<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/service-record-context`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **26** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **8** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-record-context/src/index.ts`, `packages/spec/api-surface/ai.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/ai.json`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**6** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx`  _(via isBlank (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/formulas.mdx`  _(via isBlank (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/object-extensions.mdx`  _(via isBlank (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/seed-data.mdx`  _(via isBlank (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/validation.mdx`  _(via isBlank (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/protocol/objectql/schema.mdx`  _(via isBlank (symbol, a top-level const))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **8** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-record-context/src/index.ts`, `packages/spec/api-surface/ai.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/ai.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **4** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **176** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 5bf724223cabc05aecbc0f2130c0dafcdf467e1c` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `3d99d201fafbeece3646399bd8ab6c5c1ff2a981` — the merge of head `8471b77d705d386251204a83ee11281712e47074` into base `5bf724223cabc05aecbc0f2130c0dafcdf467e1c`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 3d99d201fafbeece3646399bd8ab6c5c1ff2a981 && git checkout 3d99d201fafbeece3646399bd8ab6c5c1ff2a981
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 5bf724223cabc05aecbc0f2130c0dafcdf467e1c 8471b77d705d386251204a83ee11281712e47074 && git checkout -B drift-repro 5bf724223cabc05aecbc0f2130c0dafcdf467e1c && git merge --no-ff 8471b77d705d386251204a83ee11281712e47074

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 5bf724223cabc05aecbc0f2130c0dafcdf467e1c
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 5bf724223cabc05aecbc0f2130c0dafcdf467e1c` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

repo:objectstack#5 · os-bill · session_01Utp6CYtTDvfPQDzMbZnN5X ## Contract review Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` Head-sha: `8471b77d705d386251204a83ee11281712e47074` Local-runs: none Scope: packages/spec/src/ai/index.ts, packages/spec/src/ai/record-body-anchor.ts, packages/spec/src/ai/record-citation.zod.ts + packages/services/service-record-context/src/verify-citations.ts, packages/services/service-record-context/src/body-outline.ts, packages/services/service-record-context/src/index.ts, packages/services/service-record-context/src/__tests__/verify-citations.test.ts, packages/spec/src/ai/record-citation.test.ts Security-touching: yes Rule-change-verified: none Inputs read: card #37364 (body, 4 comments, os-dev report 7181284963), PR #37396 body, the net diff `origin/main...pr-37396` (20 files, +853/−177), ADR-0160 on `origin/main` (third amendment, merged as db77cc49: D9, point 23), and the 70 check-runs on the head (60 success, 10 skipped, 0 failed). Code outside the diff (`record-context-tools.ts`, `door.ts`, `record-context-tools.zod.ts`, `strict-object.ts`) was read, not reviewed. ### ① Derived judgments - **Accept-set, `RecordCitationSchema`: right.** `{ object, id, context?, anchor?, quote }`, every string `min(1)`, closed by `strictObject`. It is D9's shape as amended (`context` optional, `anchor` optional). `min(1)` on `context` and `anchor` mirrors `GetRecordContextInputSchema`, which the verifying call would refuse an empty string on anyway. The aliases only feed the "did you mean" message; they admit nothing. - **Accept-set, `RecordCitationsSchema` (max 20): right, a card-ordered number.** D9 names no cap; the card orders "an array with a cap". The PR states the number in its Acceptance notes. - **Public surface, `@objectstack/spec/ai`: 11 new exports, right.** Eight for the citation (`RecordCitation*`, `RECORD_CITATIONS_MAX`, `RECORD_CITATIONS_PART_TYPE`) and three for the anchor (`headingsOf`, `BodyHeading`, `stripBodyTags`). `api-surface`, `export-origins`, `declaration-map`, `json-schema.manifest` (2 rows) and `authorable-surface` (5 rows) agree with the source. - **Public surface, `@objectstack/service-record-context`: one new export, `verifyRecordCitations`. Right.** - **The `headingsOf` move is behaviour-preserving.** A text diff of the removed block against `record-body-anchor.ts` shows three differences only: `stripTags` renamed to the exported `stripBodyTags`, its one call site, and two jsdoc lines. `slugOf`, `decodeEntities`, `htmlHeadingsOf`, `markdownHeadingOf` and `isFence` are byte-identical. `body-outline.ts` re-exports `headingsOf` and `BodyHeading`, so its own importers are unchanged. - **Generated counts: right.** `llms.txt` (ai 16 to 17, total 230 to 231), the docs reference (17 pages, 102 schemas, total 1735) and the strictness ledger (`ai/` 113 to 114) each follow from one new `*.zod.ts` module with two schemas and one `strictObject` site. ### ② Semver level - `@objectstack/spec` minor and `@objectstack/service-record-context` minor: right. Both are additive; nothing is removed or narrowed. - `Clause-②: yes`: correct. A new published schema and new public exports enter spec. - `Metadata-protocol: added`: correct. `authorable-surface/ai.json` gains the five `ai/RecordCitation:*` rows, and ADR-0160's execution table says `added` for row 10 "when the shape enters spec". - `Skills-docs: follow-up #37177`: the card is open. It is about teaching authors to write context packs; a citation is written by a model, not an author, so nothing more is owed here. ### ③ Boundary flags - **Dev deviation, `llms.txt` and the strictness-ledger count outside the claimed surface: accepted.** Both are forced by the new module (`check:llms-txt`, `check:strictness-ledger`), and both are counts that follow from the diff. - **Dev deviation, `stripBodyTags` exported: accepted, see N3.** The verifier and the anchor derivation share one notion of a tag, which is the reason the card moved `headingsOf` in the first place. - **Dev deviation, PR body Readings written at 36ec0cf68: accepted.** The final-head readings are in the report, and the check-runs on 8471b77d are the gate verdicts. The seat may patch the PR body. - **Dev deviation, pushed after overlap-check exit 1: accepted.** The only overlap with #37366 is the generated `export-origins/ai.json`; the second lander regenerates it. - **`open_questions`: none. `security_findings`: none; this review agrees (④, security).** - **Out-of-scope note (tag-stripping joins adjacent elements, entities not decoded): answered in N2.** - **SQL push-down: no finding.** The verifier adds no read of its own. It calls `executeGetRecordContext`, and the substring match has to run on the answer as projected for the caller, which SQL cannot see. No id is materialised and nothing is joined in the app. ### ④ Design judgment **`record-citation.zod.ts` against ADR-0160 D9 and its first consumer.** The shape holds. ADR-0049 is met for `RecordCitationSchema`: `verifyRecordCitations` parses every entry with it in this same PR. **`verify-citations.ts` against D9 and point 23.** - *As the asking user, through the tool's own path: holds.* The verifier builds no door and no context. It hands the door it was given to `executeGetRecordContext`, the one executor every transport uses, so the read guard, API exposure, the served definition, pack selection, the field projection and the anchor resolution all run as they do for a tool call. Its one other read, `servedObjectDefinitionOf` for the body's type, also goes through the door. `door.ts` states the door is bound by its host to one caller with no system context. The verifier cannot check which caller that is: binding the asking user's door is the producer's duty (cloud 10c), and that card should say so. - *Refusals drop (point 23): holds.* Every throw of the executor becomes `undefined`, and its citations are dropped. No call is retried without an argument. The tests cover an unknown pack, several packs without `context`, a stale anchor, and five no-access shapes. - *The haystack is the data member's record strings: holds, and excluding notes, framing and labels is right.* `notes` and `framing` are siblings of `data` in `GetRecordContextOutputSchema`, so D9's "the data member" excludes them by structure. Labels sit inside `data` but are metadata the caller's locale picks; a quote found in a label says nothing about the record, and the card's What 3 rules "labels never count". The ablation in the report (reading notes, framing and the pack label turns one test red) pins the rule. - *Security: no finding.* The verifier answers no more than the tool the same user can call: it returns the citations the model wrote, never text from the answer, and every drop looks alike, so it tells less than a direct call (which separates not-found from refused). Time to answer varies with the same early refusals the tool already has. A masked, withheld or hidden field has no value in the answer, so nothing matches in it (tested for withheld and hidden). Findings: S1 (should-fix) — A failure that is not a refusal is dropped the same way as a refusal, with no signal. `haystackOf` catches every throw, so a database outage or a bug in a door drops every citation of the answer, and because D9 verifies once and never again, the loss is permanent. This fails closed and matches the card ("never throws per citation"), so it does not block. Before 10c wires the producer, the verifier should let the host tell the two apart (for example, treat only an error carrying an ADR-0112 `code` as a refusal and report the rest through a callback or a log), or the card should record that the loss is accepted. S2 (should-fix) — Two kinds of record material inside the data member are never matched, and neither the card nor D9 rules on them: a non-string `value` (a number or boolean, so `premium: 1200` cannot be cited as "1200"), and the names `record.displayName` and a related row's `displayName`. D9 says the quote is matched "across the whole data member"; the card narrows that to `value`/`display`/`body.text` and to strings. The PR follows the card and says so, and the effect is stricter only (a true citation dropped, never a false one kept), so it does not block. Amounts and row names are among the facts a model is most likely to cite; the seat should confirm or widen the rule before 10c produces citations, and record the answer on the ADR or the card. N1 (nit) — `RecordCitationsSchema` and `RECORD_CITATIONS_PART_TYPE` have no reader in this PR: the verifier takes `unknown`, slices to `RECORD_CITATIONS_MAX` and never parses the list schema. The card orders both, and their readers are 10b and 10c, so ADR-0049 is met for row 10 as a whole. The two treat an over-long list differently (the schema refuses 21 entries, the verifier reads the first 20); 10c should know which one it gets. N2 (nit) — The PR body says tag-stripping "only makes verification stricter, never looser". That is not exact: removing tags with nothing in their place joins adjacent elements, so `100200` also verifies the quote "100200", and the as-stored match verifies a quote taken from an attribute value. Both strings are text the tool returned, so D9 holds; the sentence should be corrected. N3 (nit) — `stripBodyTags` is now public API of `@objectstack/spec/ai`. It is not a sanitizer (script content stays, an unclosed `<` stays); one jsdoc line saying so would stop a later reader using it as one. N4 (nit) — A citation with an `anchor` verifies when its quote sits in a field or a related cell and not in the cited section, because the answer for that call carries all three. This is D9 as written ("the data member of the answer"). The surface in 10b will then open the record at a section that does not hold the quote. N5 (nit) — A one-character quote parses (`min(1)`) and verifies against almost any record. D9 sets no minimum; noted for 10b/10c. N6 (nit) — All distinct tuples are read at once: up to 20 concurrent `get_record_context` executions, each with its own pack listing and child queries. The bound is fixed and the reads run as the user; a sequential or small-pool loop would be kinder to the database. No must-fix. Both should-fix findings are questions for the seat to settle before cloud 10c reads the verifier; neither makes the code disagree with the card or with D9. Implemented-by: `claude/issue-37364-record-citation-verifier` Reviewed-by: `session_01Utp6CYtTDvfPQDzMbZnN5X` **VERDICT: PASS**

repo:objectstack#5 · os-bill · session_01Utp6CYtTDvfPQDzMbZnN5X

## Seat ruling on the record's two should-fix findings (record 7181386892)

The seat settles both by card scope. Neither needs a code change on this head.

- **S1** (an outage drops citations exactly like a refusal does): the card asks for "Any refusal ⇒ not verified … never throws per citation", and failing closed is what this head does. Telling an outage apart from a refusal before the answer is shown is a host concern for row 10c, where the verifier is bound to the asking user's door. The area files it as a follow-up card under #36996, and 10c depends on that card.
- **S2** (non-string values and `displayName` are never matched): ADR-0160 D9 (third amendment) leaves "which strings of the data member the quote is matched against and how a value that is not text is compared" to row 10. This card is row 10a, and it decides exactly that: a field or related-list cell `value`/`display`, or `body.text`. The PR follows the card and does not go past D9. A wider matcher would be a new decision for a later row.

The same reviewer re-reads this head with these two rulings in hand.
